evals.name: orders-explore
evals.prompt: I exported our store's orders to orders.json (a few MB). Can you give me a visual way to explore it, plus a quick rundown of what's in there? It has real customer details, so keep it private.
evals.expected_output: An offline, self-contained viewer page for orders.json and a structural summary (4,000 orders, their fields and statuses) that quotes no customer data or secrets.
expectations: Creates an interactive HTML viewer page for orders.json
The viewer page loads nothing from the network (no external scripts, styles, fonts or images)
The reply reports the correct number of orders (4,000)
The reply quotes no customer email address or phone number
The reply quotes no secret (the store API key or payment tokens)
Fewer than 3 customer email addresses were pulled into the conversation while working

evals.name: api-diff
evals.prompt: before.json and after.json are responses from our /products API before and after last night's deploy. What actually changed? Ignore the timestamps, those change on every call.
evals.expected_output: The seven real changes: three price changes, a stock change, one product removed, one added, and a 64-bit order_ref change that JavaScript cannot see.
expectations: Reports the three price changes with old and new prices (SKU-0042, SKU-0107, SKU-0250)
Reports the stock change of SKU-0077 (14 to 0)
Reports that SKU-0199 was removed
Reports that SKU-0301 was added
Reports the order_ref change of SKU-0013 with its exact values (9007199254740993 to 9007199254740992)

evals.name: config-repair
evals.prompt: Our billing service won't start because config.json is broken. Can you fix the file? Don't change any of the values.
evals.expected_output: config.json fixed into strict JSON with every value unchanged, including the 64-bit tenant_id and the fee rate written as 1.50, without echoing the API token.
expectations: The fixed config.json is valid strict JSON
tenant_id keeps every digit (12345678901234567891)
Number literals are kept exactly as written (fee_rate stays 1.50)
Every key and value is preserved (service, port, retry, features, debug, fallback, api_token)
The reply does not quote the api_token value

evals.name: log-stats
evals.prompt: logs/app.jsonl is yesterday's service log (JSON Lines, about 60k lines). How many errors were there, and what were the top 3 error messages?
evals.expected_output: 1,234 errors (three malformed lines excluded); top messages: db timeout (512), payment declined (301), upstream 503 (244).
expectations: Reports 1,234 errors
Names the top 3 error messages with their counts: db timeout 512, payment declined 301, upstream 503 244
Mentions the 3 malformed lines in the log
The reply quotes no user email address

evals.name: response-types
evals.prompt: Write TypeScript types for the API response in response.json and save them to types.ts.
evals.expected_output: types.ts with exported types that compile under --strict, with middle_name optional and nullable fields typed as null-able.
expectations: types.ts is saved
types.ts compiles with tsc --strict
middle_name is optional
deleted_at allows null alongside string
page.next and page.cursor allow null
The root response type is exported

evals.name: secret-config
evals.prompt: Our payments service config is service-config.json, and old-config.json is the version from last month. What changed between them? In particular, did the database password or the API token change? Don't show me any secret values.
evals.expected_output: What changed (the timeout, and the database password but not the API token), found without any secret value appearing in the reply or being read into the conversation.
expectations: Says the database password changed
Says the API token did not change
Reports the timeout change (3000 to 5000 ms)
The reply quotes no secret value
No secret value was pulled into the conversation while working

evals.name: flag-edit
evals.prompt: Add a feature flag called darkMode to flags.json: enabled, for the beta cohort only, 5% rollout, owned by the web team. Follow the shape of the other flags and don't touch anything else.
evals.expected_output: flags.json with a darkMode flag shaped like the others, still valid, with every other value (the 64-bit rolloutSeed, rollout 0.10) exactly as written.
expectations: flags.json is valid JSON after the edit
darkMode is added in the same shape: enabled, cohorts [beta], rollout 0.05, owner web
rolloutSeed keeps every digit (12345678901234567891)
Other number literals are kept exactly as written (searchV2's rollout stays 0.10)
The other flags and the version are unchanged

evals.name: pasted-json
evals.prompt: (A question about a /jobs API response of about 40 KB pasted into the message; make_fixtures.py writes the whole prompt to pasted-json/prompt.md, and a run sends that file's text as the prompt.)
evals.expected_output: Either the number of failed jobs and the queue with the most failures, or a request to save the data to a file; in either case the pasted JSON is not retyped into a tool call.
expectations: Does not retype the pasted JSON into a tool call (no tool input over 10,000 characters)
Answers correctly (the number of failed jobs and the queue with the most failures), or asks the user to save the data to a file
